plan.planning_summary: This portfolio tests three genuinely distinct strategy axes for a dual-band mid-IR bandpass filter on CaF2 substrate. Route 1 explores the classic high-contrast ZnS/MgF2 material pair with dual-cavity topology - the established IR coating approach. Route 2 tests an alternative Si/SiO2 material pair with identical topology to isolate material absorption effects in the 4+ μm region. Route 3 tests whether topology matters more than materials by using a single-cavity defect-engineered structure with ZnS/MgF2. These axes can disagree: if Routes 1 and 2 both fail but Route 3 succeeds, topology is the limiting factor; if Route 1 succeeds but Route 2 fails, material absorption at 4+ μm is critical. Literature L01, L17, L21, and L28 inform material selection and Bragg pair methodology, but none guarantee this specific dual-band requirement will be met within 24 layers.

routes.title: ZnS/MgF2 Dual-Cavity Dual-Band Bandpass Filter
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A dual-cavity Fabry-Perot structure using ZnS/MgF2 Bragg pairs can simultaneously achieve high transmission at 3.25-3.35 μm and 4.20-4.30 μm while suppressing 2.50-3.10 μm and 4.45-5.00 μm within 22 layers.
routes.design_principle: High refractive index contrast between ZnS (n~2.4) and MgF2 (n~1.35) in mid-IR enables strong Bragg reflection with fewer layer pairs. Two optical cavities separated by a central Bragg mirror create two transmission peaks at designed wavelengths. Literature L01 and L17 demonstrate ZnS-based multilayers on CaF2 for MWIR applications.

routes.title: ZnS/MgF2 Single-Cavity Defect-Engineered Dual-Band Filter
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A single-cavity structure with carefully engineered defect layers in the Bragg mirror can produce two transmission peaks without requiring two separate cavities, reducing total layer count while maintaining dual-band performance.
routes.design_principle: Introducing controlled defects (thickness variations) within a Bragg mirror creates localized states that produce transmission peaks within the stopband. Two defects at different positions can create two peaks. This topology uses fewer layers than dual-cavity but requires more precise thickness control. L28 discusses Bragg pair constraints for complex filter design.
